items.title: Award in Assistant Demolition Operative
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with sound knowledge of occupational health and safety working practices and acquire the competence to be able to assist to operate handheld power tools and equipment in the workplace within the building and construction sector. The candidate shall cover procedures and principles on how to assist in demolition and dismantling of existing structures manually (by hand) under supervision on construction sites.
Learning to learn how to keep updated with the content learned during the course. Communicate with colleagues and supervisors or site managers. Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction. Communicate using basic Maltese or English. Use appropriate nonverbal communication

items.title: Award in Health and Safety at the Workplace
items.description:
Aimed at providing basic knowledge to health and safety, including minimizing risk of injury, accident prevention, and other ways to improve safety at the workcation and support on construction sites.
The learner will be able to: 

- Ability to understand, interpret and apply health and safety regulation.
- Assess risk and provide consultancy on mitigating it.
- Lead individuals to a healthier and safer environment through consultancy and raising awareness of health and safety on 
  construction sites.
- Provide health and safety reports.
- Resolve disputes and improve the work environment. The learner will be able to: 

- Prevent health and safety hazards
- Understand better work environment
-Use of health and safety equipment
- Appropriately manage incidents at work place The learner will be able to: 

- Provide insight in the health and safety report
- Train on how to approach individuals who require health and safety support
- Report writing
- Basic knowledge of fire and first aid.

items.title: Award in Common Health and Safety Issues: Occupational Risk for Lone Workers,  Young Workers and Workers in Hot and Cold Environments
items.description:
The course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and awareness of specific hazards at workplace: heat and cold stress (temperature at which work becomes dangerous),  lone working (a person who works alone) and safety risks for young worker (a person under eighteen years of age who works).
Report properly all accidents,  injuries,  near-misses and other dangerous occurrences. Identify correct health and safety procedures connected with the type of working practice when someone is working alone. An understanding of the importance of personal safety for lone workers. Knowledge of the risks that a person may face as a lone worker and ways to reduce these risks. An understanding of how cooperate among workers to improve safety and health’ procedures in circumstances involving lone labours.

items.title: Award in Basic Tile Laying Techniques
items.description:
The training course is intended to give the necessary knowledge, skills and competences to someone wishing to work in the building and construction sector. It is specifically focusing on basic tile laying knowledge and skills.
Outline the preventative and remedial actions to be taken in the case of exposure to materials hazardous to health. Report any hazards which may present risk to relevant persons. Assist and perform installation of tiles under supervision. Confirm that all materials, tools and equipment necessary for the installation process are available as required. Confirm that all material, tools and equipment are fit for their intended purpose. Understand and explain the correct procedure for setting out work systems. Identify instances where additional information would be necessary and liaise with supervisor accordingly. Look for information, directions and guidance in the use of materials and tools

items.title: Award in Common Health and Safety Issues: Occupational Risk for Lone Workers, Young Workers and Workers in Hot and Cold Environments
items.description:
The course is designed to provide participants with the knowledge and awareness of specific hazards at workplace: heat and cold stress (temperature at which work becomes dangerous), lone working (a person who works alone) and safety risks for young worker (a person under eighteen years of age who works).

An understanding of how cooperate among workers to improve safety and health’ procedures in circumstances involving lone labours.

items.title: Award in Provision  for Cleaning Services
items.description:
This course is specifically designed taking into account the limitations of persons employed in the industry in terms of learning capabilities and an extremely interactive approach shall be undertaken,  with the trainer having been involved in the cleaning industry for years and owning one of the major cleaning companies in Malta. To this effect,  the students shall be embracing first-hand experience with regards to both the theoratical aspect of the course and with continuous hands-on experience reflecting the theoretical parts of the course.
1. Be conversant with the basic theoratical and practical aspects of health and safety in the cleaning industry 2. Attain basic knowledge of chemical handling 3. Identify the correct to use of cleaning machinery  4. Recognise  the importance of COSHH regulations (Control Substances Hazardous to Health) 5. Show an understanding of the use of colour codes 6. Understand the problems with cross contamination 7. Be proficient in the understanding of the difference between cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 8. Recognise the importance of correct storage of equipment and machinery. 1. Perform general duties relating to cleaning 2. Follow good working practise in relation to use of equipment and machinery 3. Determine the type of approach needed with regards to cleaning,  disinfection and decontamination 4. Access or request to all sources of information relating to COSHH regulations (Control of Subsances Hazardous to Health). 5. Provide suitable solutions for avoidance of cross contamination 6. Follow good working practices relating to correct storage of equipment and machinery 7. Access or request to sources of information relating to colour codes 8.Follow good working practices with regards to chemical handling 9. Establish clients requirements in such a manner that bridges the relationship between the employer and the client 10. Communicate and maintain a dialogue with the supervisors at work when necessary and on an ongoing basis 11. Assess which work practice is the most adequate in terms of health and safety  12. Learn both  the theoratical and practical necessities for performing the job description correctly.

items.title: Award in Waste Collection and Transportation of Waste
items.description:
Transport and disposal of municipal solid waste is one of the major environmental problems. Improper transport and disposal of municipal solid waste causes hazards to inhabitants. The amount of solid waste generated is steadily increasing and every government in this world is currently focusing on methods to approach the challenge. This unit develops good awareness of recycling activities and key statutory requirements. In addition,  learners will be more skilled at organising their workspace,  working practices and resources as well as working more effectively with each other as a team. Overall,  they will acquire the skills necessary to work more safely and efficiently.
Understand ways of mitigating potential impacts during the collection and transport of waste. Environmental Impact of Waste Management. Regulatory Policy and Legislation. Understanding the principles and procedures for waste transfer activities. Identify types of waste and arising in the Maltese Islands and relevant stakeholders. Health and Safety in the collection and handling of waste.

items.title: Award in Safe Use of Electrical Hand Held Apparatus
items.description:
This course is designed for those workers who need to work on electrical equipment who either have no electrical qualifications or need a reminder of electrical dangers and safe working practices. This course provides knowledge and skills on electrical and mechanical hazards,  on the functioning of portable tools and on the safety procedures to use at workplace.
Perform a basic risk assessment to identify the hazards specific to electrical safety,  the risks arising from those hazards,  and the control measures you should use.Achieve a visual inspection that should be carried out by the user each and every time the equipment is used,  checking for example for evidence of damage,  loose cables etc. Determine the type of approach needed to comply with safe work procedure. Apply procedures of operational maintenance. Cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the organisation of an electrical emergency in workplace. Know the general site safety,  particularly from the point of view of electrical hazards. Understand the electrical and mechanical hazards that can be encountered using an electrical tool and the precautions to be taken. Know technical and organisational preventive measures relevant to electrical and mechanical hazards in the use of electrical hand held apparatus. Know how identify and report faulty portable electrical equipment and withdraw it from service,  by ensuring it cannot be used and/or is marked faulty.

items.title: Award in Health and Safety
items.description:
The aim of this module is to provide learners with the basic health and safety knowledge and skill requirements
The learner will be able to: a) Understand health and safety requirementsb) Identify risks and hazards The Elements of the law Advantages and disadvantages of the law History of occupational health and safety Hazards caused by fire Learning the recovery position Treatment to chocking Treatment to electrical shock Sprains and strains First aid box Electrical safety Classes of fire and fire extinguishers Safety signs Health and Safety responsibilities of the employer Powers of officers

items.title: Foundation Certificate in Applied Science
items.description:
This programme of studies is aimed at giving learners the opportunity to further their studies in several diverse sciencerelated areas including environmental,  health and industrial sciences. Learners will cover various topics such as Chemistry,  Physics,  Biology,  English,  Maltese,  Mathematics and IT which will be taught in an applied manner that is relevant to the various science sectors in which employment may be sought with a higher qualification. This programme is particularly suitable for learners who have a scientific or technical aptitude,  even if they have not decided fully on their ultimate career choice.
Understand some of the factors that influence scientific progress. Describe the main factors that affect the health of individuals Make accurate scientific observations and measurements in given situations Understand what skills and qualities are required for jobs in the science sector

items.title: Award in Organic Farming
items.description:
This course will give applicants a general introduction in organic farming. Learners will understand that organic farming entails a holistic approach towards the production of food and production without compromising the future generation of production. Organic farming is sustainable and it promotes the welfare of animals. The principles of care, fairness, health and ecology are enhanced while the methods and practices applied leads to the production of food without any residues of synthetic preservatives. The philosophy of organic agriculture is against genetically modified organisms. Regards the rearing of animals no antibiotics or growth hormones are allowed on the farm. This introduction course will instill insight in the learners to comprehend, appreciate and understand organic farming and provide them with the necessary skills to start their own organic business.
Manage a horticultural unit and a poultry unit Apply a holistic approach towards organic production by embracing the principles of ecology, health, fairness and care Convert from conventional to organic practices

items.title: Award in Working in Low Risk Confined Spaces
items.description:
The objective of this programme is for those learners already working or preparing to work in industry or in any organisation where they can be exposed to confined spaces such as during construction work etc.
Topics covered in this course are regarded by the Health & safety authority  as being important in maintaining good practice in the safe, prompt and effective prevention of injuries that are in most cases fatal. The qualification provides learners with the knowledge, understanding and skills in working safely in confined spaces – medium risk
•	State the role and responsibilities for an individual carrying out work in confined space
•	Proceed to assess a task, and  select the proper rescue  equipment to use
•	Proceed to implement the emergency plan  following an incident
•	Ability to select proper PPE
•	Proceed to select the type of portable gas monitor needed for task at hand
•	Proceed to select a proper respiratory protection
•	Proceed to carry out a risk assessment and develop a rescue plan
•	State the steps to be taken to call for help and phone 112
•	Describe the safe use of a tripod  and winch used to recue injured workers
•	Describe the safe use of a  portable gas monitor
•	Describe the hazards of confined spaces
•	Describe the importance of the work permit
•	Undertake further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on working in confined spaces
•	Name and describe the effects of  the most common hazardous gasses that could be resent in confined spaces
•	Describe the effects of low oxygen concentrations
•	Describe the use and limits of various types of respiratory protection
•	Discuss with others the working procedures
•	Discuss the limitations and the appropriate application of  injured worker retrieval system
•	Discuss the fundamental components of a rescue system
•	Discuss the appropriate location and use of a tripod
•	Discuss the importance of manufacturer’s recommendations when using a portable gas monitor.
•	Discuss the limits of a gas monitor
•	Discuss IDLH atmospheres 
•	Discuss the roles and responsibilities of employers, supervisors and workers in regards to a f rescue plan and emergency procedures
Further one`s knowledge on  the importance of health surveillance and the undergoing of regular medical check ups to check fitness for the job •	Be able to list typical accidents and injuries related to working in confined spaces in the workplace
•	Be able to provide instruction to others re actions to be taken in a given situation.
•	Promote proper interaction with others so as to coordinate help during an accident.
•	Promote proper interaction  with others so as to coordinate and prepare a work plan
•	Provide suitable care and maintenance to equipment
•	Demonstrate competence in carrying out a proper work risk assessment
•	Demonstrate competence in carrying out visual inspection for equipment
•	Demonstrate competence in monitoring air quality by means of a portable gas / air tester
•	Reports and maintain records of findings and actions carried out during equipment visual inspections.
•	Convey proper information to other professionals, site supervisors etc.

items.title: Award in Basic English for Care Workers
items.description:
The objective is to help those who work in the care industry,  for whom English is not their first language,  to communicate better in a healthcare setting by improving their spoken communication,  vocabulary,  grammar and pronunciation.  An important aspect of this course will be the input of language  skills which do not necessarily pertain specifically to the caring environment but will be useful in the circumstances.
Participate in and understand the main points of discussions/explanations/instructions with potential colleagues. Interact with clients and their relatives in the course of their duties. Communicate information in a clear manner. Explain how to select an appropriate method of communication for different situations. Use the auxiliary verbs be and have got in positive,  negative and question form. Demonstrate sentence structure (positive,  negative and question form). Compose positive and negative sentences using present,  past and future tenses. . Apply appropriate vocabulary related to colours,  numbers,  food,  health,  clothes,  leisure activities,  family,  parts of the body,  likes/dislikes and express feelings. Express oneself using comparative and superlative structures. Use relevant prepositions (time/place/movement) where necessary. Use countable and uncountable nouns. Use personal pronouns in both a grammatical and lexical context.  Identify terms of address or age appropriate words and phrases depending on client groups and relatives’ state of emotion. Construct ‘Wh’ sentence question forms using present,  past and future tenses. Talk about ability using can/can’t. Express advice through the use of must/mustn’t,  do/don’t,  should/shouldn’t,  need to and don’t need  to. Use of imperative structures,  Tell the time and refer to the calendar (days/months).  Understand how to communicate effectively by using the correct grammar and punctuation in a social care setting.

items.title: Award in Beauty Therapy - Introduction
items.description:
This course covers a basic knowledge about beauty therapy with the scope of helping participants realize if they want to become internationally qualified Beauty Therapists.
It is also aimed at those who help out in a Beauty Salon and are relatives of a Beauty Salon owner – this course gives participants a good idea of the different aspects of basic Beauty Therapy.
Identify which clients are able to receive beauty treatments Describe the anatomy and physiology related to the skin Perform basic applications carried out in a beauty salon

items.title: Work Ethics and Employability Skills
items.description:
Work ethics and Employability Skills is designed to address interpersonal skills,  motivation,  initiative,  and work place etiquette. It is also aimed to provide its participants with an all rounded skills set to become more employable and most importantly; skills to enhance the chance of job retention.
Become more self-reflexive. Become more assertive and get motivated.  Work in teams and be more collaborative.  Communicate more effectively during interviews. Become more effectively communicative with colleagues at the workplace. Communicate problem solving strategies effectively and when required . Become more self-reflexive. Become aware of own learning styles. Become more motivated towards work. Identify his/her current decision making style and work at establishing more effective decision  making styles. Practice values in line with work ethics. Collaborate and work in teams. Demonstrate and advanced understanding of the rights and obligations at the workplace. Practice and apply the key principles of customer care. Engage in job searching.  Be more confident during interviews. Understand key principles of work ethics and customer care. Understand the key skills required in the workplace and master them.

items.title: Award in Assistant Limestone Block and Hollow Concrete Block Layer
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices; acquire knowledge to be able to assist in the identification of systems, equipment and components; develop knowledge and skills to be able to assist in reading of drawings and calculations with approved procedures and under supervision; and to be knowledgeable and have the skill of assisting in the laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line.
Assist in the identification of systems, equipment and components. Assist in reading of drawings and calculations. Communicate with fellow workers. Read method statements and safe works preventive measures. Apply occupational health and safety during work practices. Assist in the laying of limestone and hollow concrete blocks to line. Implement actions as per method statements and safe work practices

items.title: Award in Basic Electrical Wiring and Installation of Electrical Equipment
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices; acquire knowledge to be able to assist in the installation of electrical/electronic equipment in accordance with approved procedures; develop knowledge and skills to be able to assist in the maintenance of electrical installations and equipment in line with approved procedures and under supervision; and to be knowledgeable and have the skill of assisting in the testing of electrical installations and equipment and in the required documentation.
Identify instances where additional information would be necessary and liaise with supervisor accordingly. Look for information,  directions and guidance in the use of materials and tools Explain the key hazards associated with installation. Describe the basic principle of the equipment and circuits being installed.  Identify and describe the responsibility as an assistant electrical fitter to report and give routine handover to supervisors.  Explain the key hazards associated with maintenance and testing. Explain the reason for leakage current. Explain the purpose of final quality inspection.

items.title: Award in Achieving Excellence in Customer Service
items.description:
This course aims to go a step beyond offering learners insights into customer service.  It aims to offer learners practical tools as well as basic theoretical knowledge on how to achieve excellence when delivering customer service.
Understand how emotions effect one’s communication.  . Distinguish between the key principles of customer service in order to become more customer oriented. Be better able to deal with colleagues so as to deliver a more positive customer experience. Be better able to make a good first impression. Learn how to use different communication skills in a more effective way. Become more effective when diffusing difficult customer situations. Improve on customer etiquette. Increase customer loyalty. Become more motivated to deliver unforgettable customer service. Practice and apply the key principles of customer care. Illustrate ways of working successfully with colleagues. Identify their own communication patterns and work at improving them. Identify any barriers that are blocking effective communication and work on eliminating them. Practice emotional awareness to improve his/her communications skills. Demonstrate an understanding of the skills needed in furthering his/her communication with customers. Practice the skills needed to deal with different types of customer behaviour. Practice the skills needed to respond to diverse customer needs.Practice strategies that are in line with improving customer loyalty. Implement tips from examples of ‘best practice’ in the field of customer service

items.title: First Aid at Workplaces
items.description:
This course provides participants with a solid foundation in first aid with an emphasis on prevention,  practical skills,  decision making and dealing with environmental conditions
Handle emergency procedures and ability to administer first aid. Be responsible for evaluating the importance of emergency communication. Observe,  receive and obtain information to complete an incident report form. Identify the first aid equipment available and use it safely. Make a primary survey of a casaulty. Identify the different needs of casualities. Properly use of Automated External Defibrillator (AED). Maintain continuous professional development A sound understanding of the roles,  functions and responsibilities of a first aider. Theoretical and practical competences on first aid equipment,  including personal protection and how to use it safely. The ability to carry out incident reporting and scene survey. The ability to correctly identify  methods to manage an unresponsive casualty.Knowledge on how to administer First Aid for a range of conditions. Knowledge of the various types of casualty lifting techniques The ability to determine which type of approach is needed to perform specific scene assessments and hazard considerations. The ability to perform correct first aid practices. Determine the type of approach needed to properly apply first aid for all kind of injuries. Understand the importance of teamwork within an emergency team. Learn how to cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives. Attain a sound knowledge of prioritising and organizing which are crucial in emergency situations

items.title: Foundation Certificate in Horticulture and Animal Care
items.description:
This programme of studies is designed to equip learners with a range of basic skills and competences enabling them to become competent in various land-based activities related to the agricultural sector. This programme of studies includes a significant amount of vocational practice that will provide a clear idea of the nature of the area that the learner may wish to follow in the future. Learners will have the opportunity to gain handson experience with farm animals,  exotic animals and plants. Special focus will be given to soil,  crop and animal management,  livestock nutrition and farm maintenance.
Undertake different agricultural methods and understand the principles of health and safety Understand procedures and explore measures to improve agricultural skills Understand and apply different technical skills relating to the care of animals as well as crops. Use and apply correctly various agricultural equipment

items.title: Award in Occupational Health and Safety for General Drivers
items.description:
The rationale for this course is to equip the applicants with on-the-road health and safety skills which will guide them through the journey of enhancing their knowledge in Occupational Health and Safety. This course will support the participant in acquiring the necessary safety knowledge and to select an effective approach to undertake an action,  task or activity,  especially in challenging environments or circumstances while operating his/her vehicle.
Become aware of own learning styles. Become more motivated towards health and safety.  Identify his/her current decision making style and work at establishing more effective decision making styles. Practice values in line with health and safety. Collaborate and work in teams. Demonstrate an in depth comprehension of the importance of health and safety at the workplace. Practise and apply the key principles of health and safety. Become more self-reflective. Become more assertive and get motivated.  Work in teams and be more collaborative.  Identify key principles of Occupational Health & Safety.  Apply and master the key skills required in the workplace. Communicate more effectively with respect to Occupational Health & Safety. Become more effectively communicative with colleagues at the workplace. Communicate efficiently problem solving strategies as and when required.

items.title: VET Award Foundation in Tile Laying
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with foundational knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the tilling industry. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to follow health and safety procedures and will achieve basic skills in laying floor and wall tiles.
Describe the health and safety procedures at the workplace. Sequence the safe use of tools and associated safety precautions. Identify general paving techniques. Describe how to lay tiles in differetn simple patterns. Describe how to prepare a floor for tiling. Identify the proper tile to use according to specifications of the tiling project. Describe how to prepare a wall for tiling. Idnetify the proper tile to use accoridng to specifications of the tiling project. Plan how to execute work practices safely. Demonstrate how to identify and assess hazards at the work place and report risks to designated personnel. Demonstrate how to grout and clean tiles. Show various types of kerb such as square,  battered,  chamfered and footpath. Create appropriate mixes of mortars,  adhesives and cladding on various horizontal surfaces. Operate appropraite tools to cut,  trim,  mark and engrave tiles. Demonstarte how to lay wall tiles in simple patterns. Demonstrate the principal techniques in laying wall tiles within irregular shapes.

items.title: Award in General Occupational Healthy and Safety
items.description:
The rationale for this course is to equip the participants with workplace health and safety skills This course will support the participants in acquiring the necessary safety knowledge and to select an effective approach to undertake an action,  task or activity,  especially in challenging environments or circumstances at the workplace. Many individuals,  especially those who have been out of employment for a number of years,  tend to feel discouraged and experience a low self-esteem,  sometimes even low self-worth or a general apathy towards employment safety regulations. This course will be a motivator to encourage a healthier and safer workplace life.
Understand key terminology of Occupational Health & Safety. Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the importance of health and safety at the workplace. Become more self-reflective. Become more assertive and get motivated. Work in teams and be more collaborative. Communicate more effectively with respect to Occupational Health & Safety. Become more effectively communicative with colleagues at the workplace. Communicate problem solving strategies effectively and when required. Become aware of own learning styles. Become more motivated towards health and safety. Identify his/her current decision making style and work at establishing more effective decision making styles. Practice values in line with health and safety. Collaborate and work in teams. Practice and apply the key principles of health and safety.

items.title: VET Award Foundation in Metal Inert Gas Welding (MIG) and Metal Active Gas (MAG) Welding
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with foundational knowledge,  skills and competencies required to gain employment as a Manual Inert Gas welder. Through this training programme,  the learner will be conversant with OHS requirements for welding environments and will be able to select suitable techniques to produce basic welded joints using MIG technology and recognize the similarities between MIG and Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding.
Practice specific welding processes following  operating parameters for given types of Metal Inert Gas (MIG) / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Show the idiosyncratic similarities and differences between of Metal Inert Gas (MIG) and Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding technologies. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the flat position using Metal Inert Gas / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Metal Inert Gas / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Practice welding corner joints in the flat position using Metal Inert Gas welding / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Quote health and safety procedures and practices specific to working with working with Metal Inert Gas (MIG) / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Describe health and safety measures and precautions to prevent hazards and to ensure the safety of oneself and third parties when working  in welding environments.Describe how to weld Lap fillet joints in  the horizontal/vertical position using Metal Inert Gas / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment. Describe how to weld tee fillet joints in the flat position using Metal Inert Gas / Metal Active Gas (MAG) welding equipment.

items.title: Foundation Certificate in Hairdressing,  Beauty and Well-Being
items.description:
This programme of study provides an overview of the different routes available to learners within the Institute of Community Services,  whilst leaving all their options open. The modules on offer provide learners with basic knowledge in health and safety practices employed during beauty and hairdressing techniques and procedures. Other modules focus on an understanding of the basic scientific concepts related to all hair and beauty services and treatments,  while introducing the learners to basic business concepts. The course also provides learners with quality work experience exposure where they will be expected to assist and carry out a range of assigned tasks,  using approved models. Learners are required to purchase the necessary hairdressing and beauty accessories at the beginning of the academic year.

items.title: VET Award in Process Manufacturing
items.description:
The course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the process manufacturing industry. items.title: Award in Basic Electrical Wiring and Installation of Electrical Equipment
items.description:

This course will give a thorough understanding of tree care and the protocols that need to be followed to undertake various tasks related to optimum care of various tree species. items.title: VET Award in Principles of Gardening and Landscaping
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as a Gardner/Landscaper. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to maintain a reasonable sized garden or public garden and identify all the problems within the garden being diseses identification,  fertilization,  plant and tree identification,  irrigation and pruning problems.

items.title: Award in Medical Maltese (Part 2)
items.description:
This course is offered to BARTS University registered students aiming to work or are working/practicing in the health profession whose mother tongue is not Maltese and would like to ascertain an elementary to pre-intermediate level in Medical Maltese.

b)	Practice the use of elementary to pre-intermediate Maltese grammar to help him/her communicate in a medical context

items.title: Award in Nail Extension and Enhancement Services

items.title: Dry Stone Wall Restoration (Restawr tal-Hitan tas-Sejjieh)
items.description:
This practical course will equip learners to set out,  construct and finish a traditional rubble wall using a variety of building stones and traditional lime mortars. The importance of laying the stones correctly and the use of pinning stones will be emphasised so that no more than 30% of the volume of the wall is mortar.
Demonstrate dry wall construction techniques using appropriate tools and necessary safety precautions; Identify PPE to be used during the construction of dry walls at various rural/ surrounded by build-up areas; Carry-out a field study on an existing wall or building recording such information as the time wall was constructed,  the type of wall,  the type of stone etc; Set out using profiles and build a dry stone wall to given dimensions and specifications; Select stone that is suitable for building walls; Prepare stone to include cutting and dressing rubble stone leaving it ready for wall construction; Use a given plan to construct and erect profiles,  set out and build a coursed mortared rubble wall to include building an suitable coping of stone over the length of the wall; Use a given plan and instructions to construct and erect profiles,  set out and build a mortared random rubble uncoursed wall to include a suitable coping of stone to the tope and length of the wall; Carry out stonewall construction under supervision and in accordance with appropriate health and safety procedures. Define dry wall construction terminology; List the different type of tools used for dry wall construction; Outline the main types of traditional stonewall construction to include common features; Identify stone the three main categories of stone used in traditional stonewall construction to include the advantages for each; Read plans for traditional stonewall construction to include interpreting measurements and terminology; Set up profiles for the excavation and building of a stone foundation,  to include explain why stone projects past the wall width and why larger stones are used

items.title: VET Award Foundation in Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) Welding
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with foundational knowledge,  skills and competencies required to gain employment as a Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welder. Through this training programme,  the learner will be conversant with OHS requirements for welding environments and will be able to select suitable techniques to produce basic welded joints using TIG technology.
Quote health and safety procedures and practices specific to working with working with Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Describe health and safety measures and precautions to prevent hazards and to ensure the safety of oneself and third parties when working  in welding environments. List the operating parameters of given types of TIG welding equipment. Describe how to weld Lap fillet joints in  the horizontal/vertical position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Describe how to weld tee fillet joints in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Describe how to weld tee fillet joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice specific welding processes following  operating parameters for given types of Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Demonstrate how to use various Tungsten electrodes that are used for this specific metals being welded. Review and reinforce acquired knowledge by demonstrating how to weld simple beads on a steel plate in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice welding tee fillet joints in the horizontal/vertical position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment. Practice welding corner joints in the flat position using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding equipment.

items.title: Award in General Intensive English Course as a Foreign Language at Pre-Intermediate Level
items.description:
This Award course is designed to enhance and upgrade the participants’ spoken,  written,  reading and English listening skills through inputs of several different topics for discussion,  analysis and critical thinking.    Learning and recycling of grammar and vocabulary will occur through contextually interactive activities that will encourage learning. The programme is delivered over 4 weeks where each key area of Speaking,  Reading,  Listening & Writing is explored with the support of interactive lectures,  video discussions,  exercises,  individual and pair working together with role plays activities.  The whole programme is highly interactive and it is expected to enrich the participants’ knowledge in key all areas; sharpen their skills; and enhance their English competence.
Through the communication skills of speaking,  writing and listening,  the course will aid the students to be better able to; deal with common situations when in an English speaking country,  talk about family,  hobbies,  work,  travel and current events,  talk about experiences and events,  dreams,  hopes and ambitions,  give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans,  narrate and criticise a summary of a story from a book or film,  ask personal questions,  give and ask for directions,  talk about different personalities,  make and organise travel arrangements,  confidentally order in a restaurant,  talk about likes and dislikes,  express preferences,  make deductions and predicitions,  make offers and suggestions,  talk about obligation. At the end of the program,  the learner will be able to; Speak more fluently but accurately,  use the correct lexical jargon needed for different contexts,  use the correct grammar correctly when speaking about different contexts such as,  families,  restaurants and entertainment activities,  talk about personalities and characteristics,  giving and reading biographies,  describe Buildings,  monuments in terms of design,  texture and materials,  prediction of weather,  describe and talk about clothes and accessories,  pronounce and talk about large numbers,  be conversant with terms and phrases related to travel and tourism,  be conversant with phrases related to work and careers,  describe and talk about various hobbies,  sports and interests,  talk about the importance of Education and the benefits,  life changes and events,  talk about and criticise political beliefs,  systems and change,  talk about animals,  their extinctions,  habitats,  environment and rights,  descriptions of people,  health,  fitness and illnesses, types and likes / dislikes of music and concerts,  describe use and benefits of of household equipment.

items.title: VET Award as Assistant Plumber
items.description:
Provides the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work as a Plumber’s Assistant. This course will enable the learner to acquire the basic knowledge, skills and competences of domestic plumbing installations,  routine maintenance and repair. Persons following this course will be able to assist in the repair,  maintenance or installation of domestic plumbing installations. Furthermore,  the learner will know how to mitigate health and safety concerns at work.

Keep up to date with any changes made in the Maltese Occupational Health and Safety Act 2000. Keep up to date with any changes made to the National Occupational Standards published by MFHEA.

items.title: Health and Safety Legal Responsibilities of the Employer

Effective ways of examining workplace conditions to make sure they conform to applicable standards. Designing,  providing and maintaining a safe place of work that has safe access and egress,  and uses plant and equipment that is safe and without risk to health. items.title: Award in Safe Use of Electrical Hand Held Apparatus
items.description:
This course is designed for those workers who need to work on electrical equipment who either have no electrical qualifications or need a reminder of electrical dangers and safe working practices. This course provides knowledge and skills on electrical and mechanical hazards, on the functioning of portable tools and on the safety procedures to use at workplace.
Know the general site safety, particularly from the point of view of electrical hazards. Understand the electrical and mechanical hazards that can be encountered using an electrical tool and the precautions to be taken. Know technical and organisational preventive measures relevant to electrical and mechanical hazards in the use of electrical hand held apparatus. Know how identify and report faulty portable electrical equipment and withdraw it from service, by ensuring it cannot be used and/or is marked faulty. Perform a basic risk assessment to identify the hazards specific to electrical safety, the risks arising from those hazards, and the control measures you should use. Achieve a visual inspection that should be carried out by the user each and every time the equipment is used, checking for example for evidence of damage, loose cables etc. Determine the type of approach needed to comply with safe work procedure. Apply procedures of operational maintenance. Cooperate with co-workers and health and safety representatives in the organisation of an electrical emergency in workplace.

items.title: Award in Styling and Dressing Hair
items.description:
Styling hair by different methods is a basic and necessary skill that is an important part of the hairdressing profession
Various styling tools,  their use and maintenance; hair structure in relation to water and heat; various styling and setting products and their use in styling and shaping hair and hair types and its texture density and thickness and growth pattern The learner will be able to style and dress hair using vairous tools,  products and methods; finger dry hair,  shape hair and blow dry hair; style hair in modern,  classic and elegant styles; use products and tools to create and maintain the styles and care for tools and equipment used in styling etc Produce styles on different types of hair using different methods,  tools and products after adequate consultation; style hair according to the client's wishes and to suit the occasion; use products and tools to produce such styles; provide after care and mantain health and safety throughout all procedures

items.title: Award in Legal,  Regulatory and Organisational Requirements of a Contact Centre
items.description:
This module concerns understanding an organisation’s procedures for dealing with legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre and the legal,  regulatory and ethical limits of contact centre work.
Define health and safety procedures in a contact centre. Explain the difference between a risk and a hazard in the workplace. Describe an organisation’s procedures for raising legal,  regulatory and ethical concerns. Describe internal and external sources of information on legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements. Interpret an organisation’s procedures for dealing with legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre. Identify the legal,  regulatory and ethical limits of contact centre work. Explain the importance of following health and safety procedures to minimise risk. Summarize the scope of legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements in a contact centre. Identify how the legal,  regulatory and ethical requirements relate to a contact centre. Explain how an ‘ethical approach’ affects a contact centre.

items.title: Award in Demolition Operative (with licence to operate small mobile plants)
items.description:
This course is meant to provide the learner with occupational health and safety working practices and acquire the competence to be able to operate small mobile plants in the building and construction sector. The candidate shall be able to use further knowledge and skills to operate effectively under supervision using small mobile plant equipment on construction sites for demolition
Carry out research on the subject and units for this award. Carry out safe working practices. Find an appropriate way to reflect and evaluate their own work; seek advice,  information and support when appropriate. Communicate with colleagues and supervisors or site managers. Communicate using simple glossary terms used in the building and construction. Communicate using basic Maltese or English. Use appropriate nonverbal communication. Discuss work progress to supervisors.

items.title: VET Award in Life Skills for the Work Environment
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to gain and retain employment. Through this training programme,  the learner will be better trained and competent to use personal and social skills as well as customer care skills.
Apply learning skills and learning styles of self and others in a daily life context. Apply strategies to improve one's time management skills in a work and daily life context. Show shich aspects make up a customer care. Demonstrate how one can establish loyal customers. Identify one's learning skills and learning styles. Describe the advantages of possessing time management skills. Recall interpersonal communicative skills for the place of work. Identify verbal and non-verbal communication skills.

items.title: VET Award in Water Well Repair and Maintenance
items.description:
This course is aimed at providing the learner with general knowledge,  skills and competences required to work in the industry sector of water well repair and maintenance. Through this training programme,  the learner will be able to safely identify faults in water well systems,  undertake or advise on corrective repair procedures,  and perform maintenance procedures on water well systems.
Quote  the main health and safety procedural standards used in the sector.  List  five hazards and risks associated with workplace activities. Recite mathematical calculations related to cylindrical,  spherical and cubic volume,  ratios and proportions. Describe how pressure gauges and basic hydraulics work. Write basic water chemistry formulae and equations used to perform water quality checks. Describe the main characteristics of modern water systems,  ranging from the operator’s duties to the filtration techniques that could be used for rain water. Recall that the proper function of the wellhead is to ensure that it is not allowing the entry of surface water or foreign materials. Recall that it is important that the well cap is firmly in place and that it can withstand the weight of persons and animals. Apply on-the-job health and safety best working practises to ensure the safety of one’s self,  the safety of other persons and due care for third parties’ property. Demonstrate proficiency when dealing with GHS chemical hazard warning symbols,  hazard warning,  emergency and mandatory signs. Operate water well equipment typically used for water well repair and maintenance – much better if the equipment is specifically mentioned. Demonstrate the liabilities and responsibilities related to the proper use of such equipment. Demonstrate the affects of the process of sedimentation on water quality.  Monitor the various appropriate water filtration techniques. Show the consequence of  signs of corrosion or deterioration of the well casing. Apply appropriate techniques when looking for signs of ground settling around the outside of the well casing.

items.title: Award in Housekeeping
items.description:
The course is intended to give learners the competencies to work proficiently as Housekeepers. This qualification will provide the necessary theoretical knowledge, practical skills and competencies for learners to apply housekeeping skills in workplace. The learner will be able to understand the overall processes for adequate housekeeping.
l) Illustrate the complexities and demands of working in the hospitality industry through the scope of housekeeping.
m) Recognise and demonstrate good work practices in the provision of housekeeping services.
n) Plan and use appropriate problem solving skills in order to provide the best service possible.
o) Use appropriate Health and Safety practices and infection control protocols to safeguard oneself, colleagues and customers. 
p) Recognise, prevent and react professionally to safety risks both for the customers and the workers.
q) Develop recommendations for improvement in the upkeep of premises. 
r) Understand, and apply reflectively and critically  the main ethical principles of housekeeping. 
s) Become aware of regulations and legisation in relation to housekeeping.  
t) Propose strategies for addressing challenges which might be encourtered at the work place.
u) Works as team-member within a multidisciplinary team.
v) Communicate professionally and clearly with customers, colleagues, subordinates and superiors. a) Understand facts and procedures related to high-quality, ethical houskeeping, meet houskeeping-related challenges and recommend improvements that could be implemented to emeliorate the service
b) Assess, evaluate and interpret the role of the housekeeping department in hotel operations
c) Apply knowledge and skills to be able to carry out housekeeping duties safely, following Health and Safety practices and infection control protocols to safeguard oneself, colleagues and customers. 
d) Apply knowledge and skills to be able to communicate effectively with the front office and the engineering and the maintanance division
e) Select and use relevant knowledge to identify the typical cleaning responsibilities of housekeeping and explain how  area inventory lists, frequency schedules are carried out and utilised. f) Understand and meet the challenges associated with the housekeeping department.
g) Understand the key issues of housekeeping.
h) Understand the theoretical and practical knowledge that constitutes the work of housekeeping.
i) Describe the role of the housekeeping department in hotel operations, 
j) Explain the importance of effective communication between housekeeping, the front office and the engineering and maintenance division.
k) Identify typical cleaning responsibilities of the housekeeping department, and explain how area inventory lists, frequency schedules are carried out.

items.title: Award in Poultry Production and Husbandry
items.description:
This unit is designed to give a good understanding of the principles of laying and broiler husbandry and production. It especially targets individuals who are interested in opening a new poultry farm or who would like to update their skills to manage better an already running poultry enterprise.  This unit�s sessions are delivered in class and on a working farm and the learner will be expected to spend various hours in practical sessions on the farm. The unit will go over the basic principles of farm design and poultry husbandry including feeding,  chicken health,  slaughtering,  egg grading lighting,  record-keeping,  animal welfare and the legislation regulating this sector.
Understand basic principles of the animals� farm life-cycle and farm structure/s to accommodate this cycle. Follow agreed procedures to harvest product. Undertake tasks to follow agreed feeding regimes. Explain methods that are utilized to prevent and cure diseases and parasite infections.

items.title: Award in Providing and Maintaining Administrative Services
items.description:
The module will strengthen the general skills previously gained through training and experience of the professional manner in which administration support is provided in the office environment.
Compile a skill scan relevant to their own role. Interpret the principles of SMART goals. Describe the typical services provided by your office in the workplace.,  including:  document production,  audio transcription,  data entry,  photocopying and binding,  document control,  filing/client records management,  stationery issue and stock control,  petty cash and expenses,  reception,  dealing with incoming/outgoing mail. Explain how you comply with office management procedures including:    safe working procedures and risk assessment ,  fire,  accident and emergency,  security,   information and physical property,    resource use and stock control,  purchasing – equipment,  consumables,       service contracts,  equipment use,  monitoring and maintenance,       sending receiving and storing information,  staff movement/absence      control,  use of telephones,  internet and emails. outline techniques to monitor progress and workflow in your workplace such as:       setting guidelines,  team meetings,  observation,  checking work       products checking records/logs,  monitoring errors,  progress reporting,        delegation,  target setting. Familiarise oneself with the types of events in your workplace such as: conferences,  seminars,  promotional events,  exhibitions/trade shows,         product launches,  training courses,  team-building events. Identify steps to ensure the smooth running of an event. Including: venue/location,  fees/cost,  catering and accommodation,  publicity/advertising,  equipment,  resources,  delegates/audiencepresenters/speakers,  joining instructions,  health,  safety and emergency procedures,  activities scheduled,  information. Use smart goals to develop a personal and professional development plan that is consistent with business needs and personal objectives. Demonstrate a thorough familiarity with the principles of offering administrative services,  in various workplace situations. Identify the importance of office procedures,  evaluating and identifying any gaps in their own office procedures. Monitor progress and agreed targets in the workplace,  applying techniques explored in this module. Plan an event in their workplace with confidence. Explore principles of personal responsibilities and how to develop and evaluate own performance at work. Apply skills gained to provide professional services to your office in the workplace. Interpret and comply with office management procedures. Apply techniques to monitor and manage work flows. Organise a simulated event in your workplace within a team.

items.title: Award in Healthcare
items.description:
This course is aimed at those wishing to enter the caring profession and obtain formal knowledge and qualification in healthcare
Practise in accordance with the relevant codes of professional conduct: standards for conduct,  performance and ethics,  within the limitations of the individual's own competence,  knowledge and sphere of professional practice,  consistent with the legislation relating to healthcare practice; Work collaboratively with other practitioners and agencies; Work effectively across professional boundaries and develop professional networks; Ensure privacy and dignity of individual throughout any activity and provide care and compassion in addressing individual’s needs and concerns;  Practice in a way,  which respects,  promotes and supports individual's rights,  interests,  preferences,  beliefs and cultures; Ability to assist others within the healthcare working environment Reflect on personal knowledge,  skills and practice for continuing professional development;  Understand personal role and responsibilities in providing care; Understand the legislation and standards governing person-centred care; Understand teh meaning and importance of person centred care; Describe how to promote choice and independence; Explain how to improve care delivered to ensure person centred care

items.title: VET Award for Call Centre Agents
items.description:
This course aims at providing the learner with general and comprehensive knowledge and skills necessary in the call centre environment. It is aimed at enabling the learner to demonstrate ability in performing good customer care skills and telephone techniques.
Understand the evolution and functions of call centre. Define the role of call centre. Understand call centre systems and technology. Use call centre systems and technology to carry out service requested by customer. Understand how the system administration within a call centre functions. Familiarise with the system security management. Identify how attitude affects interaction with customers. Know how to provide requested information about produce and/or service. Define process integration. Define a problem and identify steps on how to solve the problem. Identify the purpose of a call centre. Identify the key features of a call centre. Log into the system used within the call centre that is appropriate for dealing with customers. Use tools and techniques to edit,  process,  format and present information to the customers. Perform general duties of a call centre agent. Follow good working practices. Identify the difference between an assertive and angry customer. Show how to distinguish between reacting and responding to a difficult or angry customer. Operate the calls received in accordance with organisation's protocols or procedures. Demonstrate ability to solve a problem in an effective manner.

items.title: Award in Mental Health First Aid
items.description:
Those interested in mental health and supporting individual with mental health, either at the workplace or in every day life.
The learner will be able to: 

a)	Discuss the history of psychiatric care together with the differences it has accross different cultures
b)	Demonstrate knowledge of the different classifications of mental illnesses such as mood disorders, anxiety disorders, somatoform disorders, schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders
c)	Show knowledge of the different causes of mental illness such as genetics, environment, childhood trauma, negative thoughts, stress and stressful events, drugs, alcohol, unhealth habits and brain chemistry amongst others
d)	Demonstrate understanding of how to care for individuals who have acute symptoms and which might be unstable before admission to stabilisation
e)	Demonstrate awareness of sleep disorders, sleep hygiene, psychopharmacology in adults, depression, bipolar, anxiety disorders, dementia, psychosis and eating disorders in adults
f)	Identify early onset of symptomps of dementia through the assessment of behaviour 
g)	Demonstrate ability to recognise mental health emergencies such as agression, violence, self-harm, suicide
h)	Use de-escalation techniques in a mental health crisis 
i)	Identify instances of substance misuses such as druge use and abuse, alcoholism, use of opiods, stimulants, drugs, and any other addictions such as gambling and excessive digital use
j)	Demonstrate awareness of rights and legislations governing mental health, including the rights of mental health patients
k)	Identify the factors which demonstrate challenging behaviour  and mental illnesses in children and adoloscents
l)	Plan the approporiate care of the client through the assessment of health status
m)	Discuss the indications and the implementation of the various therapeutic modalities that can be implemented with child and adolescents The learner will be able to: 
a)	Recall the istory of psychiatry
b)	Describe the local situation with regards to mental health including prevalance, services, professionals, etc
c)	Define ‘mental health’, ‘mental illness’ and discuss the different classifications according to ‘Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders’
d)	List different types of mental illnesses and the main causes of mental illnesses, conditions such as neurocognitive disorders, neurodevelopmental disorders, bipolar and related disorders, anxiety disorders, trauma and stressor related disorders, dissociative disoders, somatic symptom disorders, feeding and eating disorders, sleeping disorders, impulsive disorders, substance use and addictive disorders, psychotic disorders etc
e)	Recall the behavioural and psychological symtomps of various conditions such as neurocognitive disorders, neurodevelopmental disorders, bipolar and related disorders, anxiety disorders, trauma and stressor related disorders, dissociative disoders, somatic symptom disorders, feeding and eating disorders, sleeping disorders, impulsive disorders, substance use and addictive disorders, psychotic disorders etc
f)	Recall the best approaches to care for the mentally ill adult and the older adult
g)	List various mental health emergencies which one might come across in mental health such as agression and violence, self-harm and suicide
h)	Discuss mental health crisis and de-escalation techniques
i)	Define ‘substance misuse’ and ‘dual diagnosis’  and describe the best approaches to maange clients suffering from substance abuse
j)	Recall the best approaches for caring for individuals with intellectual disability and challenging behaviour 
k)	Describe effective approaches to care for children and adoloscents who are mentally ill
l)	Describe the role of health care workers in services for adults and for children with mental health issues within a multidisciplinary approach

items.title: Diploma in Electrical Installations
items.description:
This programme is the first stage for a learner who is interested in a career in electrical systems such as that of an Electrician within the construction industry. It contributes towards an understanding of the relevant theory and allows learners to develop the practical skills required in this field. The programme consists of twelve modules,  out of which six are vocational related and the rest are key skills related. Vocational modules focus on the basics of wiring electrical installation circuits using different cables and containment,  electrical installation regulations,  and health and safety requirements governing electrical installation processes. The rest of the modules provide an opportunity for learners to have adequate skills in Maltese,  English,  Mathematics,  Information Technology and Science and Technology.
Interpret and follow safety requirements in compliance with the law for electrical installations in construction environments Design and implement domestic electrical installations to given requirements Troubleshoot and repair existing single-phase electrical installation. Interpret wiring regulations and requirements for domestic electrical installations

items.title: Award in Sustainable Use of Plant Protection Products for Professional Users
items.description: In this course learners will be trained on the major legislation related to PPPs together with the risks and hazards related to handling,  use and storage of these products. The unit will then proceed to cover human and environmental health related to PPPs and how such products should be used safely and efficiently.

items.title: Award in Constant Watch
items.description:
The key purpose of constant watch or 24/7 observation is to provide a period of safety for patients during temporary periods of distress when they are at risk of harm to themselves and/or others. It is essential to ensure this period is therapeutic and that it is seen as a positive experience by the patient in time. It can also be used to provide an intensive period of assessment of a person's mental state. 
The purpose of this training programme is to develop participants knowledge and understanding of the clinical aspects involved in this process in order that they develop the competences and techniques to put into practice in 24/7 observation situations.

This Award has been created specifically for the needs of workers in the Health Care industry and will teach learners how to conduct 24/7 observation of patients in distress.
The learner will be able to:
a)	Demonstrate a range of techniques to assist individual in distress 
b)	Demonstrate a range of psychological and practical techniques for assisting individuals 
c)	Demonstrate techniques for the detection, de-escalation and management of aggression 
d)	Conduct a risk assessment on patient/individual Ensure environment for constant watch is safe
e)	 Practice patient centred care with awareness of patient privacy & dignity a)	Understand the relevant Mental Health legislation and regulatory framework
b)	Understand mental and psychiatric causes of mental distress
c)	Understand different levels of therapeutic observations
d)	Understand factors associated with self- harm / harm to others 
e)	Understand their role and responsibilities within healthcare team a)	Demonstrate knowledge of a range of clinical skills related to mental distress, anxiety and psychosis 
b)	Manage and engage people at risk of harming themselves or others
c)	Understand their roles and responsibilities as part of  a multi-disciplinary team in relation to supportive observations
d)	Carry out constant watch 24/7 observation within boundaries of role and according to care/treatment plan

items.title: Certificate in Food preperation
items.description: Understand and evaluate theoretical knowledge related to kitchen,  bars and restaurant operations. Create and maintain good customer and staff relations employing effective methods of communication. Comply withlegal requirements on safety,  health and hygiene.

items.title: Diploma in Welding and Fabrication
items.description:
This Apprenticeship course combines theoretical knowledge with practical training,  both in College-based industrial workshops and in industry-based apprenticeships. Learners will be expected to participate individually and in teams to fabricate welded products. Learners will have the opportunity to use hand and power tools as well as welding sets,  giving particular attention to health and safety considerations. This course also provides learners with the opportunity to further develop their knowledge of key skills subjects such as Mathematics,  Science,  English,  Maltese,  Information Technology and Individual and Social Responsibility
Identify materials and compare their properties Carry out Oxy-Acetylene Gas Welding,  Manual Metal Arc Welding and Metal Inert Gas Welding. Produce simple patterns,  developments and templates to fabricate from thin steel plates Carry out a risk assessment of the surrounding working environment before and after executing an assigned task

items.title: Award in Delivery of Customer Service for Call Centres
items.description:
This module develops students’ knowledge of key concepts of Customer Care delivery. The module covers four subject areas including:Establishing a rapport with customers in a contact centre; Supporting customer service delivery; Delivering customer service; Demonstrating knowledge of customer service in contact centres
Identify precisely customers’ needs or requests. Check understanding of customers’ needs by summarising their queries and requests. Keep records of customer queries or requests in accordance with organisational procedures. Apply organisational guidelines to deal with customer queries or requests. Summarize the standards and procedures for dealing with incidents in a contact centre. Follow organisational guidelines for greeting and identifying customers. Explain the features and benefits of products and/or services to customers in accordance with organisational requirements. Provide the required information in response to customer requests. Check customers’ understanding of the information provided.  Identify options for the resolution of customers’ queries that meet their needs. Close the customer contact in accordance with organisational guidelines. Explain the basis on which incidents should be escalated. Identify regulatory requirements when dealing with customer contacts. Describe the sources of information to be checked in order to update knowledge and understanding of organisational and regulatory requirements. Describe the limitations of the service offer that can be made to customers. Describe the limits of authority in dealing with customers. Explain the importance of checking customers’ understanding of information provide. Explain the importance of closing a customer contact in a professional way in accordance with organisational procedures and standards. Describe the standards and procedures for handling incidents. Describe techniques for controlling conversations with contacts.
